profile.headline: AI Engineer & Research Engineer | Agentic Systems | Model Training & Evaluation | Intel NCL — Office of the CTO
profile.summary:
I am a builder. I build systems and software that help research teams move faster and AI systems and the evaluations needed to tell us whether they work. My work spans language-model training, agent architectures, retrieval and context, and the engineering needed to make research reproducible.

At Intel’s Neuromorphic Computing Lab (NCL), part of Intel’s Office of the CTO, I work as an AI Engineer / AI Ops Lead. I pre-trained and instruction-tuned a 340M-parameter, 90%-sparse HGRN language model on H100 GPUs, evaluating pre-training and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with loss and perplexity, plus HellaSwag, ARC Easy/Challenge, BoolQ, PIQA, WinoGrande, SciQ, TruthfulQA (MC2) and a private, held-out instruction test set. I also worked on conversion and verification for Loihi 2 and contributed to Hala Point’s software, workloads and deployment.

Across roughly 15 years at Intel, I’ve connected research software with systems and performance engineering. I helped establish and led the Lava open-source initiative, with release and CI ownership. I built reproducible development environments and system images, plus AI-assisted engineering and independent review infrastructure across local systems and AWS. Separately, I founded and led the Agentic & AI Workgroup.

My independent projects explore how to build and evaluate capable agents:
• Syndicate: an agent organization and research platform combining durable coordination, hybrid retrieval and context compilation. Can an organized group of agents be held accountable and produce economically valuable work? Evaluation work exposed a score-scale mismatch that removed retrieved evidence before inference; controlled validation and regression coverage helped distinguish a system failure from a model limitation.
• Evolved: LLM-guided evolutionary code optimization, with sandboxed correctness and performance evaluation, experiment lineage and ablations—including documented negative results.
• Symphony: an independent implementation of OpenAI harness engineering repo designed from the initial upstream specification, extending both the specification and implementation with review, test and evidence gates, audit trails and recovery controls.

I architect and develop these projects using coding agents. My hands-on programming foundation is Python, C/C++, Java and Go; my Rust, TypeScript and Elixir work is primarily agent-assisted.

I’m in the final term of WGU’s M.S. in Computer Science, specializing in AI.

positions.title: Neuromorphic & AI Software Engineer
positions.description:
AI engineering and research software development for Intel’s Neuromorphic Computing Lab (NCL), part of Intel’s Office of the CTO, with responsibilities spanning model training, AI operations, reproducible experimentation and release engineering.
• Pre-trained and instruction-tuned a 340M-parameter, 90%-sparse HGRN language model on H100 GPUs. Evaluated pre-training and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using loss and perplexity, plus HellaSwag, ARC Easy/Challenge, BoolQ, PIQA, WinoGrande, SciQ, TruthfulQA (MC2) and a private, held-out instruction test set; contributed to conversion and verification for Neuromorphic hardware.
• Built supporting fine-tuning, model-serving and experiment-tracking infrastructure, including MLflow for experiment tracking and model versioning.
• Contributed to Hala Point through software and workload development, hardware testing, debugging and reproducible deployment.
• Helped establish and lead the Lava open-source initiative, with feature implementation, and release and continuous-integration ownership across the Neuromorphic software stack, including testing, packaging and containerized SDKs.
• Designed and built reproducible development environments, CI pipelines and system images for AI research and engineering across local infrastructure and AWS.
• Built infrastructure for AI-assisted engineering and independent cross-model review; developed agent-harness prototypes for regression triage, log analysis, reporting and testbench development.
• Founded and lead the Agentic & AI Workgroup, sharing practical approaches to agent workflows, evaluation and AI-assisted development.

positions.title: Performance Software Engineer
positions.description:
I worked enhancing performance of new OpenJDK releases and pushing patches into upstream OpenJDK.

I used C++, Assembly, Java and other languages as needed to add performant code, additional hardware instructions (SSE, AVX2, AVX512, VNNI) and new features that increase Java performance for all upstream applications that use Java.

positions.title: Cloud Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked on an edge service orchestration solution in GO Lang, using Kubernetes, Docker Containers and gRPC, API design & development, microservice design & development.

positions.title: Network Software Engineer
positions.description:
I worked on Open Network Automation Project (ONAP) and helped bring Amsterdam, Beijing and Casablanca releases to fruition by working as a committer on SDN-C, APP-C and CCSDK projects. 
Some of this work included adding a number of features, solving a heap of bugs and creating some critical path directed graphs to enable Amsterdam releases two key use cases: vVoLTE and vCPE.

Before that I worked enabling and creating containerized OpenStack extending OpenStack Kolla. Completed OpenDaylight enablement in Kolla which deploys multi-node HA ODL/OpenStack utilizing NetVirt in 15 minutes and facilitates deployment onsite at customer meetings and for evaluation, easy HA development environments and another vector for large production deploys. 

Enabling dynamic software defined networks with revolutionary flexibility in the same way hardware virtualization provided dynamic flexibility and on-demand scale for compute and storage hardware. I work on OpenDaylight (ODL), Open vSwitch, OpenStack and Open Network Automation Platform (ONAP) to enable Network Virtualization, NFV and Dynamic Service Function Chaining.

Worked in past on S3P (Security, Scalability, Stability and Performance) testing and enabling for OpenDaylight. I also contributed to enabling DPDK support for OpenDaylight. I led the S3P Workgroup in the OpenDaylight Community and I had been instrumental in the Testing and Publishing of OpenDaylight's Performance Reports 1.0, 1.1.

positions.title: Software Validation Engineer
positions.description: Test and validate Intel network drivers on Red Hat Enterprise Linux. Focus on Data Center Bridging (DCB) and Fibre Channel over Ethernet (FCoE), including user space tools (open fcoe and open lldpad). Develop automated tests and run automated regression on drivers and tools. Manage validation process, develop test plans and direct a team of testers.

positions.title: Network Storage Software Validation Engineer
positions.description: Validated network storage drivers through work with FCoE / FC / iSCSI equipment / devices such as forwarders, switches, storage arrays, and host bus adapter (HBA) / converged network adapter (CNA). Worked in Windows, Linux and virtualization (Hyper-V). Used storage and network testing tools, such as IOmeter, IOzone, dt, netperf, ntttcp, iperf, etc. Measured performance and analyzed network storage drivers and their output. Automated test cases and added features to and update automated test code base.

positions.title: Consultant - Network & System Admin.
positions.description:
Worked with business owners providing technology recommendations and budget for existing and future technology requirements. 
Supported Windows active directory domains, Windows and Linux servers plus an assortment of client PCs. Managed, maintained, supported and designed small business networks including security hardening and testing. Created physical, data-flow and use case network diagrams. Provided end user support and repair service.

positions.title: Reporter - Intern
positions.description: Wrote news pieces including front page story on Cash for Clunkers Salvage and front of section story about hiking Opal Creek. Convinced a variety of people to interview and divulge useful information. Executed an Oregon Public Employees Retirement System data analysis project supporting an investigative exposé.

positions.title: Hardware Aide - Student
positions.description: Repaired, tested and maintained enterprise Dell computer network. Setup and tested Dell and Apple computers. Networked PCs by running network cables and setting up OS configuration. Tested network with netperf, iperf.

positions.title: Computer Lab Aide
positions.description: Supported a 20 system computer lab. Trained others in the use of Microsoft Office and other complex applications. Provided personalized support.

positions.title: Computer Technician
positions.description: Built, upgraded and fixed a variety of client and server computers. Traveled to businesses and homes to fix computer and networks.
